channel.description: UN News - Global perspective Human stories | Culture and Education

item.title: Millions of children return to schools that still can’t provide clean water or a working toilet
item.description: A new academic year is underway in many countries across the world, yet millions of children still attend schools where the water is unsafe to drink, toilets are unusable and there is nowhere to properly wash their hands.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN panel calls for stronger safeguards as AI agents advance
item.description: The world's first scientific body on artificial intelligence (AI) called on Monday for safeguards to be adapted as current firewalls are “unravelling”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Guterres calls for action as hate speech spreads across new platforms online
item.description: The UN Secretary-General has called for concerted action by governments, technology companies and civil society to stamp out hate speech, emphasizing that “its toxic message is spreading fast and striking deep”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Back to school in Haiti: ‘Madame, can you stop what the gangs are doing to us?’
item.description: When UNICEF’s Representative in Haiti Geetanjali Narayan stepped into a classroom in Port-au-Prince at the start of the new school year, she asked the children a simple question: What did they most need from the UN children’s agency?
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ukraine: Attacks on education threaten an entire generation, UNICEF warns
item.description: In an underground classroom in Sumy, Ukraine, children sit quietly at their desks, busy with the day’s lessons. For the moment they are shielded from the horrors of nearly five years of war, but just barely.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Record number of attacks on education, global fund warns
item.description: While September traditionally marks the start of the school year across the northern hemisphere, a staggering 93 million children are not in class at all amid an unprecedented number of attacks on learning, education experts warned on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN tells the world: Stop making Africa look small
item.description: The UN General Assembly has voted overwhelmingly to encourage governments, schools and tech companies worldwide to stop using maps that make Africa look far smaller than it really is.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: After Israeli seizure of Kalandia training centre, UNRWA warns of impact on youth
item.description: The seizure of a vocational training centre in occupied East Jerusalem has left hundreds of Palestinian young people without access to skills and training that could help shape their futures.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan war: $22 million education boost to help 200,000 children
item.description: For millions of children in Sudan, the classroom remains out of reach as the country’s civil war continues to disrupt their education. To help tackle this huge problem, the UN global education fund on Monday announced a $22 million initiative to help 200,000 youngsters return to learning.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: What’s journalism worth in disasters and emergencies? A lot, says a new UN report
item.description: A single New York Times article on a disaster generated an additional $500,000 in official aid. That’s just one of the findings on the critical role a free press plays in saving lives, according to a new UN report released on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Afghanistan education, Myanmar flooding, Syria recovery, homecare workers in New York
item.description: Five years since the Taliban seized power in Kabul, life for some Afghans has improved while many others suffer growing hardship.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Youth advocates gather in New York to launch new AI standards
item.description: As artificial intelligence (AI) rapidly transforms everything from how we learn, to the job market, children are adopting the technology more than three times faster than adults – exposing them to unique opportunities and risks.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN calls for urgent action to protect children from online information risks
item.description: More than eight in 10 young people aged 15 to 24 worldwide are now online, and in low-income countries they outpace the rest of the population nearly two to one.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan: ‘It made me dream again’: The students refusing to let war stop their education
item.description: Sarah Tekhlu was ready to give up on university. An Eritrean refugee, she had already been displaced once from Khartoum to Madani, then again to Port Sudan, as war tore through the country around her. Higher education, she had decided, was a luxury she could no longer afford to want.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: For Brazil’s Indigenous youth, visibility is resistance
item.description: As climate change reshapes Indigenous territories across Brazil, a new generation is turning to culture and digital platforms to defend their lands and their future.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Sudan is losing another generation’ to war, Mohammed warns
item.description: More than 1,000 days of war in Sudan have left millions of children out of school, displaced or exposed to grave violations, the UN Deputy Secretary-General said on Friday, calling for renewed action to end the conflict.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Mount Olympus and D-Day beaches among new World Heritage Sites
item.description: From the peaks of Mount Olympus in Greece to the shores of the “D-Day” beaches in France, 25 cultural or natural landmarks from across the globe have been newly inscribed on the World Heritage List, updated annually by the UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Conflict and crisis put six World Heritage sites at risk
item.description: Armed conflict, insecurity and environmental pressures are threatening ancient cities, historic castles and one of the world's greatest wildlife migrations.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘I am somebody’: Street-smart youth take their declaration to the UN
item.description: When Samantha Richards and Angela Hifume walked into the Hall of Flags at United Nations Headquarters last week, they carried more than a folder of paper. They carried the voices of hundreds of street-connected children who had never expected anyone to listen.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Skills for an uncertain future: How youth can navigate a changing job market
item.description: Choosing a path for the future has never been easy, but for young people today, such rapid technological change as artificial intelligence (AI) is making it increasingly difficult to predict which skills will remain relevant in the years ahead.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: From NASA to the classroom: The engineer bringing AI to those left behind
item.description: Nia Jetter spent two decades building spacecraft and robots. Now she is trying to make sure the artificial intelligence revolution doesn't leave anyone behind.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: UN spotlights education aid solution, Sri Lanka prison violence, humanitarian aid to Venezuela
item.description: The UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) urged international lenders to expand debt-for-education swaps, warning in a Friday report that many developing countries are spending more on debt servicing than on schooling their children.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: New coalition puts children’s rights at the centre of the AI age
item.description: A new international coalition launched in Geneva on Tuesday is setting out to make sure children's safety and rights are not an afterthought as artificial intelligence reshapes how they learn, play and grow up.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Global push for AI governance amid warnings of ‘catastrophic harm’
item.description: Can artificial intelligence benefit all of humanity – safely, fairly and without causing “catastrophic harm”? That is the question at the heart of a major UN summit opening in Geneva on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘The science is here’: UN chief welcomes first global AI assessment
item.description: Fresh scientific evidence and options for harnessing artificial intelligence (AI) were unveiled Wednesday following the launch of the first global, independent scientific assessment of opportunities, risks and impacts by a pioneering UN expert panel.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Children are turning to AI for homework – and life advice
item.description: Millions of children across the globe are already using artificial intelligence to learn, solve problems and even seek advice about personal worries, while safeguards are failing to keep pace with the technology's rapid adoption.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Global learning losses threaten an entire generation
item.description: Conflict, displacement and climate shocks are disrupting education for an estimated 258 million school-aged children and adolescents worldwide, raising fears that millions risk losing not only years of schooling but future opportunities altogether, according to a new report released Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Art and culture can both fuel and counter hate, UN discussion hears on Juneteenth
item.description: From a gold collar worn by an enslaved African to music preserved for nearly a century after the Holocaust, a staged reconstruction of a hate radio broadcast or porcelain coffee cups laid out in participatory remembrance, artists in a United Nations discussion on Friday used powerful images to underscore how culture can shape the fight against hatred.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UNESCO launches consultation on fair payment for news in the digital age
item.description: UN cultural agency UNESCO has launched a global consultation process to inform its Draft Guidance on Fair Compensation for News, particularly as online platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly rely on journalistic content.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ukraine: Latest Russian attack kills civilians, damages cultural landmark
item.description: Several civilians were killed and dozens more were injured in the latest wave of overnight attacks in Ukraine that targeted the capital Kyiv, the city of Kharkiv and the country’s history and cultural heritage, the United Nations said on Monday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
